Why I am keeping this journal

Journal / August 16, 2026 / 3 min

I forget things. Give it six months and the details of something I built go soft at the edges; a year later I can only tell you that I solved it, not how. The understanding does not survive on its own — it survives if I left a reference behind.

So that is what this is. Working notes, closer to a lab notebook than a blog: what broke, what I misunderstood, and what I would do differently. Public, because it is harder to hand-wave a step when a reader could ask about it.

A deliberate detox

Writing this is also how I detox from AI. Not because the tools are bad — they are genuinely useful, and I use them. But reaching for one the moment a problem gets uncomfortable is how I stopped noticing that I had quietly outsourced the thinking. Sitting with a problem until I actually understand it is a muscle, and it weakens fast when something else lifts for me.

Using an AI tool is good. Letting it do the part I should be doing is not — at least not from where I stand.

So the ideas here are mine. Every entry starts from something I built, broke, or read closely enough to have an opinion about, and anything borrowed gets credited in the references. I may use a tool to tighten a muddled paragraph or push me to explain a step I skipped, but the understanding comes first and the tool comes after.

Thoughts, or something I got wrong? Send me a note .
